comments.text_zh: 补充一下…… 虽然我没参与过 Clojure 的贡献流程，但我觉得有意思的是，Brian Goetz 六个月前在 Conj 上的主题演讲讲的是 stewardship，尤其是对 Java 语言的 stewardship：[VIDEO] 这让我更好地理解了使用一门语言或提交补丁的人，与设计和维护一门语言的人，所关注的问题是不同的。在日常工作中，我会使用 Clojure 之外的语言，我非常怀念那种内聚而优秀的设计。Brian Goetz 的演讲一针见血地说明了为什么我日常用的那些语言是次优的，即使它们眼下正是「新宠」……至少目前是这样……
comments.text: To add on to that... Even though, I haven't been involved in the contributing process for Clojure, but I thought it was interesting that Brian Goetz's keynote at the Conj 6 months ago was about stewardship, in particular, stewardship of the Java language: [VIDEO] It gave me a better appreciation for the differing concerns of someone using a language or contributing a patch vs. someone designing & maintaining a language. In my day-to-day, I use languages other than Clojure, and I sorely miss the cohesive and good design. Brian Goetz's talk nails it on the head why the languages in my day-to-day are sub-optimal, even if they're currently the "new hotness"... at least for now...

comments.author: gw
comments.why_zh: 关于在不破坏东西的前提下演进平台的精彩演讲。
comments.quote_zh: 如果你想看关于这个主题的精彩演讲
comments.text_zh: 我违背了自己的判断做了次反向图片搜索，找到了你截取那张图的原帖[1]。帖子里全是人们在经历自动软件更新器会带来的那类典型问题，还有 Jeff 给出的如何用 SSH 和 git 手动更新的说明。这种事就是会发生。世界是混乱的，不管是技术能力不足，还是常见的软件更新器 bug，Web 后端不会总被更新。正如你指出的，这最终可能导致安全问题，我同意——但这并不能成为故意破坏他们代码的理由。说他们被破坏是合理的，因为他们反正迟早会被 0wned，这论点简直达尔文主义得离谱。回答你最后一个问题：更新 Web 这样的系统，方式正是我们一直以来用的方式—— accret​​ion（渐进积累）。极少数例外之外，90 年代初的网站今天仍然能工作。我们引入 flex box 时并没有移除 `table` 标签。我们在保留现有功能的同时添加新 API。如果你想看关于这个主题的精彩演讲，去看 Brian Goetz 的《Stewardship: The Sobering Parts》[2]。很值得花时间。[1] [LINK] [2] [VIDEO]
comments.text: Against my better judgement I did a reverse image search and found the post that you found that screenshot from [1]. The post is full of people having exactly the sort of problems you would expect from an automatic software updater, along with instructions from Jeff on how to manually update using SSH and git. These things happen. The world is messy, and whether due to technical inadequacy or run-of-the-mill software updater bugs, web backends will not always be updated. As you've noted, this could eventually lead to security problems, and I agree -- but that doesn't justify intentionally breaking their code. To say that their breakage is justifiable because they'll be 0wned at some point anyway is an absurdly darwinian argument. To address your last question, the way you update a system like the web is exactly the way we always have -- accretion . With very few exceptions, websites from the early 90s still work today. We didn't remove the `table` tag when we introduced flex boxes. We add new APIs while preserving existing functionality. If you want to see a fantastic talk on this exact subject, watch "Stewardship: The Sobering Parts" by Brian Goetz [2]. It is well worth your time. [1] [LINK] [2] [VIDEO]

comments.text_zh: 而你说的“telling”，我想你是指随着时间推移，Java 一直非常审慎地演进，尊重向后兼容性；或者说，一项特性一旦进入这门语言，就很可能在未来 25 年里一直留在那里。是的，创新非常重要（而且现在有了 6 个月的发布节奏，创新比以往更快），但大部分工作不在于决定把什么加进去，而在于决定把什么挡在外面；以及如果某个东西确实被加进去了，它如何同时满足“慢慢来，别搞坏”和“快点，我们想要新特性”这两类受众。关于这个过程的一个好视频：[VIDEO]
comments.text: And by telling I think you mean that over time Java has very thoughtfully evolved in a way that respects backwards compatibility, or that once a feature is in the language it'll very likely stay there for the next 25 years. Yes, innovation is very important (and happening faster than ever now with the 6-month release cadence), but a majority of the work isn't in deciding what goes in, it's deciding what stays out and if something does go in how does it satisfy both audiences of "move slow don't break" and "move faster we want features". A good video on this process: [VIDEO]

comments.author: kevindamm
comments.text_zh: 早在 2002 年的一份最初提案里就提到过这件事 [LINK]，但那个链接看起来已经失效，也没有 Wayback 存档……如果我没记错，基本上是因为 JVM 的某些部分会利用 stack unwinding 来判断是哪些用户态代码在调用某些系统代码……而且当前栈帧带有锁状态的元数据，这些元数据用于支持可重入锁；如果你把整个递归调用省略掉，就会丢失它们（最初的提案就是这么做的：只删除那几条用于建立调用栈帧和从其中返回的 bytecode 指令）。2016 年左右一个更非正式的提案允许 soft tail calls 和 hard（带注解的）tail calls，并带有一些限制，显然是为了避开系统调用以及锁/重入维护方面的问题：[LINK] 还有一个视频，是 Oracle 的一位 JVM 架构师讲为 Scala 加入 TCO [VIDEO]。另外，HN 之前也介绍过一种做法，通过使用 goto 而不是严格删除 bytecode 指令来避免安全问题：[LINK]
comments.text: It was raised in one of the initial proposals, back in 2002 [LINK] but that looks like a dead link and no wayback archive.. IIRC, basically it's because some parts of the JVM use stack unwinding to figure out what userland code is calling certain system code.. also the current stack frame has metadata about lock status used for allowing re-entrant locks that you lose if you elide the entire recursive call (which the initial proposal did by only removing the few bytecode instructions that set up the callstack frame and return from it). A more informal proposal from ~2016 allows for soft tail calls and hard (annotated) tail calls, with some restrictions that evidently avoid issues with system calls and lock/reentry maintenance: [LINK] And a video by one of the JVM architects at Oracle about adding TCO for Scala [VIDEO] Also previously featured here on HN, a way to do it that avoids security concerns, by using goto instead of strictly deleting bytecode instructions: [LINK]
